description: The final format of a Unity game: its released repo and its dataset. Prose: docs/game-format.md. Validator: tools/validate-game.py (repo + dataset contents) with tools/validate-dataset.ps1 (dataset layout). Severity: error = not in the format; warning = a quality rule or something to look at.

repo.what: the game's git repo at its release commit (tracked files only)

required_files.what: the game's scenes; everything the game is made of is under Assets/, store packs included, every file with its .meta
every editor step that ran, kept unchanged
Visible Meta Files (Unity keeps the mode here since 2020.1, VersionControlSettings.mode; EditorSettings' m_ExternalVersionControlSupport is the old, obsolete place)
headless Unity runs through the heavy-job limiter, from the template
the creation record; every row matches docs/schemas/workflow-row.schema.json (unity-workflow/v0)
hero image + captioned gallery of real gameplay stills
every external asset; matches docs/schemas/assets-manifest.schema.json, every listed file committed
Git LFS for every binary type, Unity YAML as text
Unity's generated folders, build output and the local dataset zip

never_tracked.what: Unity's generated folders and build output are never committed
Unity regenerates the IDE projects on every open; they hold machine paths
a Unity licence file is a secret

m_SerializationMode.what: Force Text: scenes, prefabs, materials and ScriptableObjects commit as diffable YAML

m_Mode.what: every asset's GUID and import settings live in its committed .meta

repo.lfs_why: every binary type of templates/unity-game/.gitattributes goes through Git LFS (Unity data that stays binary under Force Text, lighting, terrain and NavMesh data, by path under Assets/: ProjectSettings/NavMeshAreas.asset is YAML); Unity's own YAML and C# stay plain git text so they diff and merge (an .asset may go to LFS through a pattern of its own when Unity writes it in binary; one that is YAML in LFS is an error). Binary content under any other name in plain git is a warning.

meta.what: every tracked file and folder under Assets/ and under an embedded package Packages/<name>/ has its .meta tracked, and every tracked .meta has its file or folder (a folder is tracked when a file under it is); names Unity skips on import (.name, name~, cvs, *.tmp, and everything under them) need none
meta.why: the .meta holds the GUID every scene, prefab and material refers to the asset by: an asset without it gets a new GUID and its references break; a .meta without its asset (or of an empty folder, which git cannot hold) is an orphan Unity deletes

banned_names.what: never inside a game: tool, vendor and owner names (text files of the repo; LFS and binary files are scanned by the packager)

account_name.what: the account (user) name of the machine running the validator, as a word (USERNAME at run time; machine paths carry it): never written in the repo
account_name.why: user decision (b), 2026-10-15: enforced in workflow.jsonl and every other non-script file; scripts and editor steps that already ran (Scripts/, Assets/Editor/Steps/, and .ps1/.psm1/.py/.sh/.bat/.cmd files anywhere) stay unchanged and are scrubbed at packaging

repo.dataset_folder: Dataset/ (variant repo-dataset): checked as a dataset when manifest.json is there; a game that is not packaged yet has none (python tools/package-dataset.py <slug> writes the folder)
tasks: Tasks/<game>-<kind>-<slug>.json, one GameTask each (game-task/1: docs/schemas/game-task.schema.json), on the repo's orphan branch `tasks` (no shared history with main; a short README.md, optionally tasks-workflow.jsonl), never on main; the name field equals the file stem

the tasks branch is checked out as a git worktree outside the game folder (e.g. <root>/tasks/<slug>) and committed and pushed there; task work never enters the game's history: main tracks nothing under Tasks/ and never references the tasks branch, the recording hooks ignore commits on it, and the delivered history (History/) leaves it out
the validator and the packager read the tasks from `tasks`, else `origin/tasks`; a missing tasks branch is an error
at least 5 and up to about 10 per game (fewer than 5 is an error; more than 10 is reported, never an error or warning)
at least 4 of a game's tasks are hard (fewer is an error); the others may be medium (what a task that names no difficulty is, the schema's default), none easier

seed.game is the repo's slug; seed.commit and seed.reference are commits of main's history (ancestors of main's head) or of the task's own start branch starts/<task name>; at both, ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt names Unity 6000.3.x (a start opens as committed, never upgraded)

every task is a long thread of multiple edits: never easy, tagged long-thread, with seed.reference, at least 3 required outcome probes outside still_works, and from seed.commit to seed.reference at least 5 game files (Assets/, Packages/, ProjectSettings/; an editor step or a .meta is not one), 100 code lines and 2 systems, and for a seed on main 4 commits that change the game (tools/validate-game.py); everything a no-op passes weighs 0

An agent given a task starts from a history-less snapshot of the game at seed.commit with Tasks/, History/ and Dataset/ removed (they hold every task's rubrics and references): only the brief and that snapshot. The grader's half (milestones: rubrics, judge and code-judge questions, log_absent patterns; and seed.reference) never reaches the agent.

dataset.layout: docs/dataset-layout-v1.json (unity-dataset-layout/v1); tools/validate-dataset.ps1 picks the file by manifest.layout
manifest: game equals the zip's top folder (full variant)
every files[] entry exists with that size (sha256 checked by validate-dataset.ps1)
totals.files = number of files[]; totals.bytes = sum of their bytes
status complete: pending empty, replay_verification present with pass equal to report.json verdict.pass (PASS or FAIL: the verdict is metadata, the replay is required but need not pass)
replay_verification is null only while ReplayScripts/ is pending (listed in pending): the delivery is then pending, not invalid
variant full: build is an object; repo-dataset: build is null
commit equals the last commit in git.log and report.json final_commit
workflow: every line is one JSON object matching the row schema
a row's direction names an earlier op user.direction row
user.direction rows: actor user, reason_source user_direction, params.direction a non-empty string

the person's directions are user.direction rows, written by the session (the sessions' prompts and replies themselves are in History/sessions/messages.jsonl); a game with none is reported as a warning

banned names in rows: workflow.jsonl is append-only except that a row naming a banned term is edited in place to a neutral word or placeholder, nothing else changed, followed by one appended row op "log.correct", params {rows: [ids], what}; the commit names the edited rows (tools/scrub-workflow-rows.py). A banned name left in a row is an error, in the repo and in the dataset.
history: full variant: manifest.history is an object; History/<game>.bundle is a git bundle whose refs include history.head = manifest.commit
the bundle holds every commit (history.commits); git.log lists the same commits
every Git LFS pointer in every commit has its object under History/lfs/objects/<aa>/<bb>/<sha256>, and each object's sha256 equals its name (history.lfs_objects / lfs_bytes count them)
author and committer of every commit are dev_NN; commit messages carry no banned names (the repo's patterns; the packager's rescan also covers every text blob)

History/sessions/ (optional): messages.jsonl (every prompt the person typed and every reply the model wrote: time, session_id, role user | assistant, text) and actions.jsonl (every tool call: time, session_id, event), one JSON object per line, rows up to the release commit, each session named session_NN in both files; manifest.history.sessions counts their rows ({messages, actions}, each {file, rows}); a missing file is a note, anything wrong here a warning, never an error
brief: Brief/brief.md (the original brief) and Brief/design.md (design doc, story bible, status) are present and non-empty; manifest.brief names them
tasks: full variant: Tasks/README.md and, per task, Tasks/<name>/task.json (the agent's part) and Tasks/<name>/grader.json (milestones, seed.reference); manifest.tasks lists the names
task.json holds no milestones and no seed.reference; task.json merged with grader.json is valid against docs/schemas/game-task.schema.json
each task's name equals its folder; seed.game is the dataset's game; seed.commit and seed.reference are commits of History/<game>.bundle
at least 5 and up to about 10 per game; at least 4 of them hard; the others may be medium (what a task that names no difficulty is), none easier
repo-dataset: no Tasks/ (the repo's tasks branch is the source)

An agent given a task starts from a history-less snapshot of the game at seed.commit with Tasks/, History/ and Dataset/ removed (they hold every task's rubrics and references): only the brief and that snapshot. The grader's half (milestones: rubrics, judge and code-judge questions, log_absent patterns; and seed.reference) never reaches the agent.
